findings.description: The reports bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects written to it (including the vendor-roster.xlsx seed object) receive no explicitly configured at-rest encryption, unlike the audit bucket in the same configuration.
The ledger exports bucket, which holds financial export data, defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving ledger data without an explicitly enforced at-rest encryption control.
The model artifacts bucket defines versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored model artifacts have no explicit at-rest encryption requirement.
The operational runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving its contents without explicitly configured at-rest encryption.

acl = "log-delivery-write" grants the S3 log delivery group write and ACL-read access to the audit bucket, a broader grant than a pure log sink requires and one that weakens the integrity of the destination that also receives model_artifacts logs.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for the audit bucket (or any bucket here), and it carries a non-private, log-delivery-write ACL, so nothing prevents objects or ACLs from being made publicly accessible.

The vendor-roster.xlsx seed object is written into aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive, which has no server-side encryption configuration, so this third-party vendor data is persisted without explicitly enforced encryption at rest.
